about.title: A neighbourhood clinic, run the way one should be
body: Kamalakar Clinic sits right at the bus stop on Mount Poonamalle Road, opposite Sabari Sagar and a short walk from Madha Nagar — a location chosen so that getting to a doctor never has to be the hard part of getting well. For the households and working families of Mugalivakkam, this has meant a general physician within easy reach for everyday illness, ongoing conditions, and the kind of routine check-ins that are easy to postpone when a clinic feels far away.

The clinic is named for its founding doctor, and that founder-led character still shapes how it runs — a small, attentive practice rather than a large impersonal one. Patients are seen by the same physician visit after visit, which matters most for the ongoing management of things like diabetes and blood pressure, where a doctor who already knows your history is worth more than a fresh set of questions each time.

We've kept the clinic straightforward on purpose: walk-ins are welcome, evening hours mean a visit doesn't have to cost you a day's wages, and the near S&S, Madha Nagar landmark means most autos and buses along Mount Poonamalle Road already know exactly where to stop.

blogPosts.title: Why Seeing the Same Doctor Matters for Diabetes & Blood Pressure
blogPosts.excerpt: Chronic conditions like diabetes and hypertension aren't a one-visit problem — here's why continuity with a single general physician makes such a difference.
blogPosts.author: Dr. Kamalakar Reddy
content: Diabetes and high blood pressure aren't conditions that get solved in a single visit — they're managed, month after month, through small adjustments to medication, diet, and monitoring. That kind of management works best when the doctor making those adjustments already knows your history, rather than starting from scratch at every appointment.

At Kamalakar Clinic, patients with chronic conditions tend to see the same physician visit after visit. That continuity means fewer repeated questions, faster recognition of what's changed since your last reading, and a treatment plan that actually evolves with you instead of resetting each time.

It also means catching small changes early — a blood pressure reading trending upward over three visits tells a very different story than a single high reading in isolation, but only if the same doctor is tracking both.

None of this replaces specialist care for complicated cases, and we refer onward when that's genuinely needed. But for the everyday management that most diabetes and blood pressure patients need, a familiar doctor at a familiar clinic on Mount Poonamalle Road covers most of what the year actually requires.
